headline: Centre agrees Parliament debate on NEET, accuses Rahul of shifting stand
content: New Delhi, July 22: The Centre on Tuesday said it is prepared to hold a discussion in Parliament on all issues relating to the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) and the student movement linked to the examination, even as it accused Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi of shifting his demands after initially seeking a debate.Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) Jitendra Singh said the government had accepted Rahul Gandhi's demand for a parliamentary discussion on the NEET issue, but alleged that the Congress leader later insisted on the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan as an additional condition."The government is ready to discuss in Parliament all issues related to NEET and the associated movement," Singh said in a statement, adding that Gandhi's conduct was "contrary to every norm of democracy" and did not befit the Leader of the Opposition.The statement came hours after Jitendra Singh, accompanied by Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, met Rahul Gandhi at the protest site outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, where the Congress leader, party president Mallikarjun Kharge and other senior leaders had staged a dharna demanding the Prime Minister's resignation over the police action against students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak.According to Singh, the government had requested Gandhi to call off the protest as the location was not designated for demonstrations and the sit-in was causing inconvenience to the public.He said Gandhi had initially conveyed that he would withdraw the protest if the government agreed to discuss the NEET issue and the associated student movement in Parliament. After obtaining approval from the government's top leadership, Singh said he informed Gandhi that the demand had been accepted.However, Singh alleged that Gandhi subsequently added a fresh demand, seeking the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in addition to the parliamentary debate.The Minister also claimed that the Congress had not submitted any formal notice seeking a discussion on the NEET issue in Parliament, despite demanding one publicly.Later in the evening, Delhi Police removed and detained Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and several other Congress leaders from the protest site.The controversy over the NEET examination and the alleged paper leak has become a major political issue, with the Opposition pressing for accountability and action from the Centre, while the government has maintained that it is willing to debate the matter on the floor of Parliament.PTI
